text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Four UMNO youth members who participated in an unlawful assembly which disrupted last November's Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor will be charged in the magistrate's court on Friday.
-- Malaysia is heading towards becoming a centre for new innovations in view of its rapid development in information technology, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says.
-- The Cabinet Committee on Foreign Workers urges those employing illegal immigrants to surrender them by Saturday when the amendments to the Immigration Act is enforced.
-- An in-house investigation by Bank Bumuputra Malaysia into an attempt to cheat the bank of 1.5 billion ringgit in October last year found that its staff were not involved.

-- Malaysia will lodge an official protest against the U.S. Federal Communications Commission's proposed cap on the amount American telephone companies pay to local firms for international calls from the U.S.
-- The government will amend the laws to enable the authorities to charge owners of night-spots where patrons are caught abusing drugs in their premises, Mahathir says.
-- Mahathir defends Malaysia Airlines against accusations of poor service.
